question: Under the Rajasthan Homestay (Paying Guest House) Scheme 2026, what is the maximum number of rooms permitted per unit?
solution:
The correct answer is __**8 rooms.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **The Government of Rajasthan launched the Rajasthan Homestay (Paying Guest House) Scheme 2026 to promote rural tourism, decentralise tourism growth, and boost self-employment opportunities.**
 
• **The scheme is aligned with Ease of Doing Business, Ease of Living, Deregulation 2.0, and tourism decentralisation strategies.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• Maximum room capacity per homestay unit has been increased from 5 to 8 rooms under the 2026 scheme.
 
• Maximum bed capacity has been enhanced to 24 beds, allowing greater accommodation flexibility.
 
• The scheme is implemented state-wide across Rajasthan with immediate effect.
 
• The registration process is fully digital through a one-window online system with reduced documentation requirements.
 
• Temporary registration is granted within 7 working days, enabling immediate operations.
 
• Permanent registration is issued after inspection and remains valid for 2 years.
 
• Deemed approval provision applies if the registration certificate is not issued within the stipulated time frame.
 
• Mandatory owner residence requirement has been removed, allowing flexible management.
 
• Properties can be managed by the owner, lessee, or a designated caretaker.
 
• Registrations can also be processed at local Tourism Department offices and Tourist Reception Centres (TRCs) to ensure rural accessibility.
 
• Two categories of registration are introduced:
 
 
• Silver Category: ₹1,000 registration fee with basic facilities.
 
• Gold Category: ₹2,000 registration fee with priority processing and mandatory enhanced amenities such as AC/heating, internet connectivity, upgraded furniture, smoke detectors, and security systems.
